title: Latency Faro oddity scan (personal run)
content:
Goal:
- Quick exploratory run to see whether a staggered coldstart pattern (randomized small bursts interleaved with idle periods) produces a persistent p99 uplift vs steady Poisson arrivals on the same capacity. Lightweight, reproducible notes for follow-up.

Background / why this matters:
- We keep seeing occasional 10-20% p99 bumps when traffic has short idle windows (3-15s) followed by small bursts. Hypothesis: GPU context/KV cache priming + runtime thread wakeup + RPC channel cold penalties combine. Need to characterize shape and persistence.

Hypothesis:
1) Short idle gaps cause partial eviction/soft-cold conditions leading to higher tail for next ~50 requests.
2) If bursts are randomized in amplitude/timing (not periodic), the p99 effect spreads across time and can be mistaken for non-deterministic jitter.

Setup (quick):
- Model: redwood/llm-small-v1 (float16 baseline) and quantized variant q4_0
- Region: us-west-2 (dedicated dev-pool node)
- Node: 1xA10G equivalent (dev-only host)
- Runtime: current main (kernel-selection patch from PR 1123)
- Clients: single-node loadgen (wrk-style harness) on separate host
- Concurrency: keep concurrency=8 for all runs
- Sequence length: 64 tokens output requested, prompt lengths random 20-40 tokens
- Arrival patterns tested:
  a) Poisson baseline at 55 qps (steady)
  b) Staggered-random: repeat cycles of idle windows [3s, 7s, 12s] chosen uniformly, then burst of 6–20 requests over 1s; average qps ~55
  c) Deterministic short-idle: 10s idle, 8 requests in 1s (for contrast)
- Run length: 30 minutes per pattern (discard first 3 minutes as warmup)
- Sampling: full per-request latency logged, plus periodic memory/KV stats from /metrics endpoint every 5s.

Commands used (approx):
- start loadgen: ./loadgen --pattern staggered-random --qps 55 --concurrency 8 --duration 1800 --out lat_faro_staggered.csv
- collect metrics: curl http://node/metrics > metrics_staggered.prom (every 5s via cron)

Quick raw numbers (median / p95 / p99 in ms) — first pass:
- Poisson baseline:  median=32ms, p95=78ms, p99=140ms
- Staggered-random: median=35ms, p95=92ms, p99=210ms
- Deterministic short-idle: median=36ms, p95=105ms, p99=260ms

Observations / notes:
- Staggered-random shows a clear p99 uplift (~50% worse than Poisson). Median is slightly higher but stable.
- Deterministic short-idle is worse than randomized in p99, suggesting synchronous evictions or batched GC-like effects when everything wakes simultaneously.
- Trace sampling (10% sampling) during staggered run shows many of the tail traces have "KV cache miss" events and runtime thread stalls ~1-3ms each (not single catastrophic event but several small stalls adding up).
- Metrics: GPU memory usage dips briefly during idle windows (~80% -> 62%) then climbs back; KV cache hit ratio drops after idle windows for ~20s.
- There are occasional small increases in CPU sys time on the host ~200–300ms shortly after bursts, correlating with RPC channel reestablishments in the trace.

Tiny ASCII p99 timeline (staggered run, 30s snap):
- timeline (s):   0  5 10 15 20 25 30
- p99 (ms):      110 130 160 140 180 205 190

Interim conclusion:
- Short idle windows (3–12s) are enough to produce persistent p99 degradation for tens of seconds after the burst. Not a single spike but a raised tail.
- Likely culprits: KV cache demotion/eviction policy + lightweight RPC reconnects + runtime task wakeups. Combined effect multiplies.

Quick experiments to try next (cheap):
- Increase background pinning of KV cache between runs (force keep-alive priming) and see p99 delta.
- Add a small preflight noop request (0-token) 100ms before burst to pre-warm paths — measure benefit.
- Run same staggered-random against quantized q4_0 variant to see whether compute reductions change tail shape (maybe less kernel variance).
- Try concurrency=16 to see if higher concurrency amplifies or masks the tail.

To-dos / notes-to-self:
- Upload lat_faro_staggered.csv + sampled traces to /s3/tmp/daphne/lat_faro/ (done).
- File a short issue in GH with findings + link to PR1123: GH-issue draft (title: "staggered idle pattern -> p99 uplift investigation") — assign to Rowan for follow-up on KV cache policy.
- Check with SRE whether node-level TCP keepalive / gRPC channel settings are non-default for dev pool nodes.

Open questions / variant hypotheses:
- Is there a threshold idle duration below which no p99 uplift occurs? (try 1s, 2s in next run)
- Does a sequence of ultra-short idle gaps (e.g., 0.5s) cause same effect due to scheduler sleep/wakeup penalties?
- Could runtime kernel selection be oscillating after idle periods causing small intermittent slowdowns?

Random stray notes:
- Noticed a small correlation between prompt size (longer prompts) and more pronounced tail — might be due to KV prefetch widening. Needs controlled test.
- The PR1123 kernels patch had a small change to attention tiling that could increase initial kernel selection time; pinged @Rowan to double-check if that lines up with observed timing.

If I had 1 hour I would:
- Run preflight-noop + staggered-random side-by-side (15min each)
- Collect traces at 100% for 2 minutes around a burst peak to get full view
- Try q4_0 variant for direct compare

Okay that's it for now — this is a personal scratchpad. Will tidy into a short GH issue and a reproducible harness later.

-- daphne
